what_happened: The job to give OLY-B-NOTE-01 a specialization mechanism, measure and tests was rejected at the final verdict. Two of 7 acceptance criteria were unmet. Criterion one: running `athena status --snapshot` on the real records should show a `specialization` block that lists each class of work, with per-setting job counts summing exactly to the dispatched request jobs that have a producer invocation, counted from history.json and recorded invocations. Criterion two: the same command before and after should leave the landing time, throughput, keep rule and planning cost lines unchanged, with landing time within a few minutes taken from commit times. The verifier also gave two major findings and no blockers: behavior criteria 4 and 5 are unmet because their evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). No checks are listed as failed.
cause: Nothing required a new status measure to be replayed on the real records and compared with independent sources before the job counted as done. The criteria needed real-records runs checked against counts from history.json that the change does not compute. The producer's evidence did not cite commands that actually ran (D43), and nothing before the final verdict checked that. The same status-measure family of jobs, including the identical NOTE-01 job in the previous case, keeps failing this way, and the producer was not told this recurring gap.
other_causes: The criteria set an exact-match target (0 difference) against a figure the change does not compute, which depends on the producer running a separate cross-check.
Retries of this family are queued without carrying over the earlier rejections' lesson, so the same evidence gap recurs.
open_hypotheses: The measure might actually give counts that differ from history.json. The fields only say the evidence was missing or unmet, not what the real output was.
The producer might have run the commands but failed to cite them. The fields cannot separate not running from not citing.
prevention: Add a standing step for any job that adds a status measure. Before the verifier runs, the step runs `athena status --snapshot` on the real records and compares the new measure with an independent count from history.json and recorded invocations. It also compares the unchanged status lines before and after. It writes the commands and outputs into the evidence file, so the behavior criteria can cite commands that ran (D43). Reading-stage guidance for status-measure jobs should say to do this. This would have prevented the whole class, because the replay and the cross-check would be built in, not left to the producer.
proposed_request: Give OLY-B-NOTE-01 a specialization mechanism, a `specialization` block in `athena status`, and tests. Outcome: `athena status --snapshot <evidence directory>` run on the real records lists each class of work with per-setting job counts, and those counts sum to the number of dispatched request jobs that have a producer invocation, as counted independently from history.json and the recorded invocations. Acceptance: (1) Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence directory>` and record the exact command and output in the evidence. (2) Separately compute the expected count from history.json and the recorded invocations with a command that is also recorded, and show the two numbers are equal. (3) Run the status command before and after the change on the same records and show the landing time, throughput, keep rule and planning cost lines are byte-identical. (4) A new test fails on the base tree and passes with the change. (5) Each behavior criterion's evidence cites the commands that actually ran (D43). (6) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test pass. (7) Add the CHANGELOG.md entry.
